finding:
Partial landing. For a<b and a second-countable Hausdorff locally compact abelian R_{>0}-modulated G, §1.1.3 calls W_I^{s,2}(G) the completion of the all-weight S_E(G) and asserts without proof that the same norm completion is obtained from S_[a,b](G). The norm squares the modulus of the function, multiplies by max(|g|_G^(2a),|g|_G^(2b)) times (1+|log|g|_G|²)^(s/2), integrates against a fixed Haar measure and takes the square root. No s range is stated on p. 11; the later definitions specify real s≥0. The later compact radial formula has exactly these weights and dt/t; the general compact formula uses canonical Haar. The equal-completion statements of Lemmas 9.2.2.2(1) and 9.2.2.10(1) concern an open J containing I, not the endpoint-only extension to S_I asserted on p. 11. Section D.3.6 offers a compact-support density route in the finer topology; its displayed radial Leibniz step drops the cutoff in the top-derivative term, and the resulting estimates omit its tail and the polynomial factors in ordinary logarithmic Schwartz seminorms. These defects are not counterexamples to the norm-completion claim.

The new Lean module proves the identity-module G=R_{>0} case for normalized dt/t. It uses Masullo.logWeightedProfiles (Icc a b) and Masullo.logWeightedProfiles univ from the accepted Proofs/Theorems/RadialWeightedSchwartzStage.lean at base 6f1d672bc14e2f53d6fc17f45019bf1b61e64e8b, with all the specified weights and actual SchwartzMap factors, not an extra exponential-decay condition. Endpoint polynomial Schwartz bounds prove integrability of the exact squared norm. The weighted L² maps are complex-linear and faithful on the original continuous profiles. The checked bridge to the literal positive-real integral uses Masullo.map_volume_exp_eq_restrict_realMultiplicative in Proofs/Theorems/RealMultiplicativeMeasure.lean at the same base. Compactly supported smooth radial cutoffs of each closed-interval profile belong to the all-weight space; domination by the original integrable squared norm yields convergence in that same norm. Thus the two images have the same complete closure in weighted L², giving a common isometric completion in a concrete ambient space. This works for any real s and permits a=b; a>b is excluded because Icc would not provide either endpoint. This neither proves fine-topology compact-support density nor formalizes the completion equality for nontrivial norm-one kernel and arbitrary fixed Haar measure. It does not claim that the closure is the whole ambient L² or construct an equivalence between abstract completion types. See .godel/formalize/radial-hardy-sobolev-completion.md for the source/proof comparison and ordinary-import replay.
retry: For the general group passage, identify the actual Schwartz–Bruhat profile stage on each admissible G/k, and derive endpoint uniform bounds with arbitrarily high inverse powers of 1+|log|g|_G| from its Schwartz seminorms. Check pushforward of arbitrary fixed Haar under the proper surjective log-module as c dx with finite c>0, and multiplication on each profile stage by a smooth bump in log|g|_G with support in a compact module window. Prove the resulting smooth compactly supported profile belongs to S_E(G) at that stage. These bridges give an integrable endpoint majorant and the same weighted L² dominated-convergence argument without assuming the printed LF density proof or a tensor-stage identification.
